other.label: CBO cost estimate: H.R. 1346, Nationwide Consumer and Fuel Retailer Choice Act of 2025

summary: H.R. 1346 amends the Clean Air Act to permit the year-round sale of gasoline blended with 10% to 15% ethanol (E15) by updating Reid Vapor Pressure waiver rules and nullifying certain state-level exclusions. It also modifies the Renewable Fuel Standard Program by altering compliance requirements and exemption petitions for small refineries, directing the return of certain compliance credits for specific past years, prohibiting the reallocation of certain waived volumes, requiring an EPA rulemaking on fuel infrastructure and labeling, and establishing a new exemption process for qualifying small refineries at risk of closure.

affected_groups.effect: Allowed to sell gasoline blended with 10% to 15% ethanol year-round and subject to updated EPA labeling and storage tank rules.

Receive a 75% reduction in compliance requirements starting in 2028, have standard exemption petitions terminated after 2027, become eligible for the return of certain past compliance credits, and gain a new targeted exemption process if at risk of closure.
affected_groups.group: Small refineries and small refining companies

affected_groups.effect: Existing state exclusions from the Reid Vapor Pressure waiver submitted after January 1, 2022, are nullified, with the ability to submit new requests after enactment.

Tasked with returning specific credits, administering the modified RFS requirements, prohibiting certain obligation reallocations, and finalizing new fuel infrastructure and labeling regulations within 18 months.

key_provisions: Applies the Reid Vapor Pressure waiver for 10% ethanol-blended gasoline to gasoline blended with 10% to 15% ethanol, allowing year-round sale of E15.

Nullifies existing state exclusions from the Reid Vapor Pressure waiver submitted after January 1, 2022, while allowing states to submit new documentation after enactment to seek exclusions going forward.
Defines a small refining company based on a daily average aggregate production limit of 75,000 barrels per day for calendar year 2025.
Terminates standard small refinery exemption extensions and petitions beginning in calendar year 2028, and reduces small refining companies' compliance requirements by 75% starting in 2028.
Directs the EPA to return certain retired compliance credits to eligible small refineries for compliance years 2016, 2017, and 2018 under specific circumstances.
Prohibits the EPA from reallocating to other persons any renewable fuel obligations applicable to small refining companies whose compliance requirements are reduced.
Requires the EPA to finalize a rule within 18 months modifying E15 fuel dispenser labeling and underground storage tank compatibility regulations.
Creates a petition process for qualifying small refineries facing imminent risk of closure, permanent idling, or conversion due to compliance costs, subject to specific volume caps.
missing_information: Economic costs and benefits of year-round E15 sales and RFS changes.
Environmental or air quality impact assessments regarding the expanded E15 waiver and nullification of state exclusions.
The total number of small refineries or companies that will qualify for credit returns or the 75% compliance reduction.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 1346 amends the Clean Air Act to permit the year-round sale of gasoline blended with 10% to 15% ethanol (E15) by updating Reid Vapor Pressure waiver rules and nullifying certain state-level exclusions. It also modifies the Renewable Fuel Standard Program by altering compliance requirements and exemption petitions for small refineries, directing the return of certain compliance credits for specific past years, prohibiting the reallocation of certain waived volumes, requiring an EPA rulemaking on fuel infrastructure and labeling, and establishing a new exemption process for qualifying small refineries at risk of closure.
summary_detail.significance: The bill changes national fuel marketing by enabling year-round sales of E15 gasoline and significantly restructures compliance obligations and relief mechanisms under the Renewable Fuel Standard Program for small refineries over the coming years.
